endorsements.quote: In critical-care early warning, physicians need more than a risk probability; they must understand why the algorithm makes its prediction.

unlisted_practices: Design AI early-warning monitoring systems to use patient-specific, adaptive warning thresholds and abandon one-size-fits-all thresholds.

Have AI risk models prioritise and assign the highest weight to GFR calculated with the CKD-EPI 2021 combined creatinine-cystatin C equation rather than accepting Cockcroft-Gault-derived EHR GFR values.
Have AI monitoring algorithms automatically recalibrate warning thresholds and down-weight heart rate variability when negative chronotropic agents such as beta-blockers are detected.

Have AI monitoring systems suppress the heart rate variability module upon detecting atrial fibrillation, frequent premature ventricular contractions, or paced rhythms, and rely on other metrics instead.
Incorporate digital continuous-monitoring technologies into future revisions of oncological care standards and clinical guidelines for febrile neutropenia.
Add specific reimbursement provisions for continuous remote physiological monitoring of oncology patients on highly myelosuppressive regimens.

Conduct large multicenter decentralized randomized clinical trials of continuous monitoring plus explainable AI, using endpoints such as unplanned ICU admission, alert-to-needle time, and early mortality.
Embed individual baseline risk from real-world evidence subgroup analyses as prior probabilities in monitoring algorithms to improve specificity and reduce alarm fatigue.

screen.reason: This is a Perspective article that mines pharmacovigilance databases and proposes a conceptual framework/recommendations for continuous physiological monitoring coupled with explainable AI to detect neutropenic sepsis.
